title: Hierarchically semi-separable matrix approximation from two-sided matrix-vector products
summary: Approximate an arbitrary real square matrix by a matrix with nested HSS bases, measured against the best HSS squared Frobenius residual.

description_paragraphs: Return a quasi-optimal HSS approximation relative to the best HSS matrix on the same tree.

model.instance: Arbitrary real $N\times N$ input with public HSS comparison class.
model.parameter_domain_description: Public integers $L,k\ge1$, $N=2^{L+1}k$, and target factor $\gamma\ge c_{\mathrm{HSS}}L$ for a sufficiently large universal constant. The fixed binary partition has $2k$ indices per leaf.
description_paragraphs: The hidden input $A$ is arbitrary. The comparison class uses a perfect binary tree with $2^L$ leaves of size $2k$.
An HSS matrix has a telescoping factorization $B^{(L+1)}=B$, $B^{(1)}=D^{(0)}$, and $B^{(\ell+1)}=U^{(\ell)}B^{(\ell)}(V^{(\ell)})^{\mathsf T}+D^{(\ell)}$ for $\ell=1,\dots,L$.

At level $\ell$, $U^{(\ell)}$ and $V^{(\ell)}$ have $2^\ell$ diagonal blocks of shape $2k\times k$ with orthonormal columns. $D^{(\ell)}$ has $2^\ell$ arbitrary diagonal blocks of shape $2k\times2k$. The base $D^{(0)}$ is arbitrary $2k\times2k$.

proofs.title: Adaptive Gaussian leaf-block exact recovery
proofs.body: Choose $A$ with only one nonzero diagonal leaf block of size $2k\times2k$, with independent standard Gaussian entries. Such a matrix lies in $\operatorname{HSS}(L,k)$ by using that block in $D^{(L)}$ and setting the other $D$ blocks to zero. The relative guarantee therefore requires exact recovery almost surely for every fixed $A$. Condition on the private seed. At each adaptive query, remove the known components in the spans of previous left and right queries. Conditional on the transcript, the unseen part of the leaf block on the two orthogonal complements is again a standard Gaussian matrix in transcript-measurable orthonormal coordinates. This follows inductively from orthogonal Gaussian conditioning: a fresh right or left query reveals one column or row of the current residual, and the remaining entries are independent. With fewer than $2k$ total queries both complements are nonzero, so the conditional law retains a continuous component and no transcript-measurable output can recover it exactly. Integrating over the seed and the Gaussian instance contradicts per-instance exact recovery.
proofs.scope: This local proof uses the paper's HSS definition and covers every adaptive randomized exact two-sided query algorithm.

evidence.supports: Batching across levels by block nullification, fresh sketches, and the expected squared residual bound.
